links.outcome: Exact three-run reproducibility of LLM outputs across repeated queries
links.effect: Exact three-run stability was 45.0% for primary classification, 48.3% for safety-critical status, and 28.3% for the full four-domain score profile across 60 vignette–platform combinations.
links.quote: Across 60 vignette–platform combinations, exact three-run stability was 45.0% for primary classification, 48.3% for safety-critical status, and 28.3% for the full four-domain score profile.

links.outcome: Composite success of LLMs versus early-career urologists on the same vignettes
links.effect: Primary composite success was 70%, 64%, 60% for LLMs versus 85% and 89% for urologists (Cochran's Q = 34.23; P < 0.001); safety-critical errors 25-26% vs 1-2%.
links.quote: Primary composite success was achieved in 70/100 (70.0%) GPT-5.2, 64/100 (64.0%) Claude, and 60/100 (60.0%) Gemini responses, versus 85/100 (85.0%) and 89/100 (89.0%) for Urologists A and B (Cochran’s Q = 34.23; P < 0.001).

links.outcome: Safety-critical errors in LLM responses to oncology vignettes
links.effect: Safety-critical errors occurred in 25.0%, 25.0%, and 26.0% of LLM responses versus 2.0% and 1.0% of urologist responses (Q = 51.34; P < 0.001).
links.quote: Safety-critical errors occurred in 25.0%, 25.0%, and 26.0% of LLM responses versus 2.0% and 1.0% of urologist responses (Cochran’s Q = 51.34; P < 0.001); all six human–LLM contrasts remained significant.

unlisted_practices: Use safety-gated endpoints and repeated-query stability alongside conventional accuracy measures in LLM evaluation

screen.reason: The study conducts a source-masked clinical vignette benchmark comparing LLMs to early-career urologists to evaluate diagnostic/management accuracy, safety-critical errors, and stability across repeated queries, but does not test an organizational deployment practice or guardrail.
